question: When is an employer required to transfer an employee to another job for health-related reasons?
answer: The employer must transfer an employee who has, according to a medical opinion, lost the ability to continue their previous work for a long time, or who is prohibited from doing it because of an occupational disease or its threat, or has reached the highest permissible workplace exposure set by the competent public health authority.

evidence.title: Act No. 311/2001 Coll., Labour Code
evidence.quote: the employee, due to his/her state of health, has lost the ability to continue performing his/her previous work for a long time, according to a medical opinion, or if he/she is not allowed to perform it due to an occupational disease or the threat of this disease, or if he/she has reached the highest permissible exposure

question: What details about meetings must be included in an agreement establishing a European Works Council?
answer: The agreement must specify the venue, number and duration of the European Works Council’s meetings.

evidence.title: Act No. 311/2001 Coll., Labour Code
evidence.section: § 245a Agreement on the introduction of a different procedure for informing and
evidence.quote: the venue, number and duration of European Works Council meetings,

question: When is an employee exempt from reimbursing the employer for the costs of vocational training?
answer: The employee is not obliged to reimburse the costs if a medical opinion says they cannot perform the profession they trained for, the employer breaches its obligations under the employment contract, collective agreement, or legal regulations, or the employer terminates the employment relationship, except in the specified cases.

evidence.title: Act No. 311/2001 Coll., Labour Code
evidence.section: § 53 Conclusion of an employment contract with a secondary vocational school
evidence.quote: The employee is not obliged to reimburse the employer for the costs under paragraphs 2 and 3 if: cannot, according to a medical opinion, perform the profession for which he was preparing

question: From May 1, 2018 to April 30, 2019, what was the minimum hourly wage benefit for work on Sunday under the first listed rule?
answer: At least 50% of the minimum wage per hour in euros.

evidence.title: Act No. 311/2001 Coll., Labour Code
evidence.quote: Section 122b (1) at least 50% of the minimum wage in euros per hour pursuant to a special regulation,

question: When can an employer terminate an employee because of redundancy?
answer: An employer may terminate an employee if a written decision by the employer or competent authority changes the employee’s tasks or technical equipment, reduces the number of employees to improve work efficiency, or makes other organizational changes. For a temporary employment agency, termination of a temporary assignment before the agreed end of a fixed-term employment relationship can also make the employee redundant.

evidence.title: Act No. 311/2001 Coll., Labour Code
evidence.quote: the employee becomes redundant due to a written decision of the employer or the competent authority on a change in his/her tasks, technical equipment or on a reduction in the number of employees in order to ensure work efficiency or on other organizational changes

question: Can an employer refuse a request for shorter hours from a parent who permanently cares for a child under 15?
answer: The employer must comply unless serious operational reasons prevent it. If the employer refuses, they must give the reason in writing.

evidence.title: Act No. 311/2001 Coll., Labour Code
evidence.quote: the employer is obliged to comply with their request, unless serious operational reasons prevent this. The employer must justify the refusal of the request under the first sentence in writing.

question: How much notice is required to end an agreement assigning an employee to a shared job?
answer: Either the employer or the employee may terminate the agreement in writing. It expires one month after the termination notice is given, unless they agree otherwise.

evidence.title: Act No. 311/2001 Coll., Labour Code
evidence.section: § 49b Transition to another form of employment
evidence.quote: The agreement on the assignment of an employee to a shared job shall expire one month after the date of notification of the termination of the agreement, unless the employer and the employee agree otherwise.

question: What is the maximum number of overtime hours an employer may order an employee to work in a calendar year?
answer: An employer may order an employee to work overtime for up to 150 hours in a calendar year.

evidence.title: Act No. 311/2001 Coll., Labour Code
evidence.quote: An employee may be ordered to work overtime up to a maximum of 150 hours in a calendar year.

question: What minimum compensation is an employee entitled to for each hour of inactive on-call time outside the workplace?
answer: The employee is entitled to at least 20% of the minimum wage in euros per hour.

evidence.title: Act No. 311/2001 Coll., Labour Code
evidence.section: § 96a Work availability with flexible working hours
evidence.quote: For each hour of inactive part of on-call time outside the workplace, the employee is entitled to compensation of at least 20% of the minimum wage in euros per hour

question: For an employee posted from another EU country to Slovakia who replaces someone doing the same work at the same location, what previous posting time counts toward the 18-month threshold, and what must a Slovak employer include in an agreement when posting a domestic employee to another EU country?
answer: The replacement’s posting time includes the replaced employee’s posting time. The Slovak employer must agree in writing on the posting’s start and end dates, the type and brief description of the work, the work location, and the wage conditions.

evidence.title: Act No. 311/2001 Coll., Labour Code
evidence.quote: If a visiting employee replaces another visiting employee who performed the same work task at the same location, the duration of posting for the purposes of the first sentence shall also include the duration of posting of the replaced visiting employee

evidence.title: Act No. 311/2001 Coll., Labour Code
evidence.section: § 54b Change of working conditions and terms of employment due to posting to
evidence.quote: the domestic employer shall conclude a posting agreement with the domestic employee, in which it shall agree in particular on: the start and end date of the posting, the type of work during the posting and its brief description, place of work during the posting, wage conditions during posting.

question: What is an employee generally required to do about instructions from superiors, and when may refusing work or an instruction not be treated as a failure to fulfill that duty?
answer: An employee must carry out superiors’ instructions when they are issued in accordance with legal regulations. However, an employer may not treat refusal to work or comply with an instruction within the time specified in the preceding sentence as a failure to fulfill an obligation.

evidence.title: Act No. 311/2001 Coll., Labour Code
evidence.quote: work responsibly and properly, carry out instructions from superiors issued in accordance with legal regulations

evidence.title: Act No. 311/2001 Coll., Labour Code
evidence.section: § 53 Conclusion of an employment contract with a secondary vocational school
evidence.quote: The employer may not consider it a failure to fulfill an obligation if the employee refuses to perform work or comply with an instruction within the time specified in the first sentence.

question: How long does the Office have to decide whether to grant accreditation?
answer: The Office must decide on granting accreditation within 90 days from the day the proceeding is initiated.

evidence.title: Act No. 18/2018 Coll. on personal data protection
evidence.quote: The Office shall decide on granting the accreditation up to 90 days from the day of initiation of the proceeding.

question: How often must prosecution offices check whether processed personal data are still needed for their tasks?
answer: The General Prosecutor's Office, in cooperation with other prosecution offices, must verify this at least once in 12 months.

evidence.title: Act No. 18/2018 Coll. on personal data protection
evidence.quote: The General Prosecutor's Office in cooperation with other prosecution offices shall verify at least once in 12 months if the processed personal data are still needed for completing the tasks of the prosecution.

question: How quickly must a controller notify the Office about a personal data breach, and is there an exception?
answer: The controller must notify the Office no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of the breach. This does not apply if the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights of a natural person.

evidence.title: Act No. 18/2018 Coll. on personal data protection
evidence.section: Section 40 Notification of a personal data breach to the Office
evidence.quote: Controller shall notify the personal data breach to the Office no lat er than 72 hours after having become aware of it; this shall not apply if the personal data breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights of a natural person.

question: How quickly must an accredited monitoring body notify the Office in writing about changes related to its accreditation?
answer: It must notify the Office in writing within 15 days from the date of the change.

evidence.title: Act No. 18/2018 Coll. on personal data protection
evidence.quote: notify the Office in writing of any changes of the granting accreditation within 15 days from the date of a change

question: If I ask the Office to verify whether a competent authority lawfully processed my personal data, how long does it have to tell me the results or explain why it did not carry out the verification?
answer: The Office must inform you within 30 days of receiving your request for verification, either of the results or of the reasons why the verification was not carried out.

evidence.title: Act No. 18/2018 Coll. on personal data protection
evidence.quote: informs the data subject about the results of the verification within 30 days of the date of submission of the request for verification , or of the reasons why the verification was not carried out

question: When may special-category personal data be processed for scientific research, and what is the purpose of a personal data protection proceeding if someone alleges that processing violated the law?
answer: Such processing may be carried out for scientific research purposes when the interests are appropriate to the objective, respect the essence of personal-data protection, and include specific safeguards for the data subject’s fundamental rights and interests. A proceeding determines whether rights or data-protection rules were infringed and, if deficiencies are found and it is reasonable and useful, may impose corrective measures or a fine.

evidence.title: Act No. 18/2018 Coll. on personal data protection
evidence.section: Section 16 Processing of Special Categories of Personal Data
evidence.quote: processing is necessary for archiving purposes, scientific, historical research purposes, or statistical purposes under this Act, special regulation, or international treaty binding upon the Slovak Republic, wh ich interests are appropriate with regard to the followed objective, respect the essence of the law protecting personal data, and lay down appropriate and specific measures to safeguard fundamental rights and interests of the data subject.

evidence.title: Act No. 18/2018 Coll. on personal data protection
evidence.quote: The purpose of personal data protection proceeding (hereafter as “proceeding”) is to determine whether there was any infringement of the rights of natural persons when their personal data were processed or if there was any violation to this Act or a special regulation2) in the area of personal data protection; and, if any deficiencies are identified, if it is reasonable and useful, to impose corrective measures or impose a fine for violation of this Act or a special regulation2) for the area of personal data protection.

question: Which types of crane operators must hold a valid license, certificate, or authorising document?
answer: Operators of mobile cranes of boom type and tower cranes of boom type must hold a valid license, certificate, or authorising document.

evidence.title: Act No. 124/2006 Coll. on occupational health and safety
evidence.quote: person operating mobile cranes of boom type and tower cranes of boom type

question: How far in advance must an authorized legal entity announce the date, time, and place of a verification of expertise?
answer: It must notify the National Labour Inspectorate or publish the information on its website at least 15 days before the verification begins.

evidence.title: Act No. 124/2006 Coll. on occupational health and safety
evidence.section: Section 14 Verifying the Fulfilment of the Requirements for the Safety of Technical Equipment
evidence.quote: The authorized legal entity is obliged to notify the National Labour Inspectorate or publish on its website the date, time and place of verification of expertise at least 15 days before its commencement

question: During the period from 1 May 2010 to 31 December 2011, which employers could have a doctor or public health care professional perform the specified occupational health care duties?
answer: They could do so for an employer employing fewer than 50 people performing work in category one or two, or work placed in category two.

evidence.title: Act No. 124/2006 Coll. on occupational health and safety
evidence.section: Section 39b Provisions on the Changes Effective as of 1st May 2010
evidence.quote: In the period of 1st May 2010 - 31st December 2011, a doctor or a public health care professional pursuant to section 26, par. 3, may also perform the duties of occupational health care pursuant to section 26, par. 1, letter a) to d), letter e) of the first point and letter g) for the employer, who employs less than 50 persons performing the work placed in category one and two or performing the work placed in category two.

question: After learning about a registered occupational accident, how soon must an employer send the accident report, and to whom?
answer: The employer must send the report within eight days of learning about the accident to the competent labour inspectorate or supervising authority and to the injured employee, or to their bereaved if the employee died.

evidence.title: Act No. 124/2006 Coll. on occupational health and safety
evidence.quote: send the report of the registered accident to the following parties within eight days from acquiring knowledge of occupational accident given: 1. the competent labour inspectorate or the competent supervising authority, 2. the employee having suffered the registered occupational accident, or to their bereaved, if the employee died as a result of the occupational accident given

question: If a licensed worker seriously breaches occupational safety rules and the breach results in an accident causing severe bodily harm, what must happen to the worker’s licence, and what must the employer do about the accident?
answer: The labour inspectorate must withdraw the worker’s licence, and the worker may apply to have it reissued no earlier than one year after the withdrawal decision becomes legally effective. The employer must report the serious accident without delay to the competent labour inspectorate or supervisory body, investigate it with an authorised safety technician, and prepare an accident report within four days of being notified.

evidence.title: Act No. 124/2006 Coll. on occupational health and safety
evidence.quote: If the natural person holding the licence, certificate or document pursuant to paragraph 1, letter b) seriously breached or repeatedly acts in conflict with the legal and other regulations pertaining to occupational health and safety in connection with their professional activity performance, the relevant labour inspectorate shall withdraw their licence, certificate or document pursuant to paragraph 1, letter b).

evidence.title: Act No. 124/2006 Coll. on occupational health and safety
evidence.quote: in the event of death, severe bodily harm (hereinafter referred to as the ‘serious occupational accident’), the employer shall ask an authorised safety technician to participate in the investigation

question: Until the increased basic compensation rates take effect, what rate applies to two-wheeled vehicles, three-wheeled vehicles and quadricycles?
answer: The rate established for one-wheeled vehicles and tricycles applies until the increased rates take effect.

evidence.title: Act No. 283/2002 Coll. on travel allowances
evidence.quote: Until the application of the increased amounts of basic compensation determined under this Act as amended from 1 January 2025, the amount of basic compensation for two-wheeled vehicles, threewheeled vehicles and quadricycles shall be the amount of basic compensation established by the measure pursuant to paragraph 2 for one-wheeled vehicles and tricycles.

question: When did the Act come into force, and was any provision subject to a different date?
answer: The Act came into force on 1 July 2002, except for Section 21, which came into force on 1 January 2003.

evidence.title: Act No. 283/2002 Coll. on travel allowances
evidence.section: § 40 If, pursuant to Section 8 as amended until 31 December
evidence.quote: This Act shall enter into force on 1 July 2002, except for Section 21, which shall enter into force on 1 January 2003.

question: What is the maximum insured amount for which an employee can claim reimbursement of moving insurance expenses?
answer: The employee can claim reimbursement of proven insurance expenses for the transported property up to a maximum insured amount of 400 euros.

evidence.title: Act No. 283/2002 Coll. on travel allowances
evidence.section: § 22 Reimbursement of expenses for moving personal
evidence.quote: The employee is entitled to reimbursement of proven expenses for insurance of the total value of the transported property up to a maximum insured amount of 400 euros.

question: When may an employer provide compensation based on an amount it recognizes rather than documented expenses?
answer: If the law requires the employee to prove expenses and the employee fails to provide that proof, the employer may provide compensation in an amount it recognizes, taking into account the specified conditions of the business trip.

evidence.title: Act No. 283/2002 Coll. on travel allowances
evidence.quote: If this law requires proof of expenses and the employee fails to provide them, the employer may provide him with compensation in the amount recognized by him, taking into account the specified conditions of the business trip

question: When an employee is posted to an EU country and their accompanying spouse voluntarily pays social insurance premiums, what reimbursement may the employee receive for those premiums, and what compensation applies during the posting?
answer: The employer reimburses the spouse’s demonstrably paid premiums for the posting period, retroactively for the previous calendar year and subject to the stated monthly limits. The employee is entitled to compensation on the same basis and in the same amount as for a foreign business trip, unless the host country’s law provides more favourable compensation.

evidence.title: Act No. 283/2002 Coll. on travel allowances
evidence.section: § 26b Reimbursement of expenses for social insurance and
evidence.quote: the employer shall pay the employee the sickness insurance premium, old-age insurance premium, disability insurance premium, solidarity reserve fund premium, unemployment insurance premium or old-age pension savings contribution demonstrably paid by this person for the period of the employee's temporary posting retroactively for the previous calendar year.

evidence.title: Act No. 283/2002 Coll. on travel allowances
evidence.quote: If the employee is posted to a Member State of the European Union, 7a ) he is entitled to compensation to the extent and amount of the same as for a foreign business trip, unless he is entitled to more favourable compensation under the law of the Member State of the European Union to which he is posted.

question: What is the maximum supplementary payment a professional soldier may receive for particularly important or extremely demanding cybersecurity work?
answer: A professional soldier may be awarded a supplementary payment of up to 90% of their salary.

evidence.title: Act No. 69/2018 Coll. on Cybersecurity
evidence.quote: may be awarded a supplementary payment for special activities of up to 90% of his/her salary.

question: By when must operators of essential services newly included in the registry adopt security measures?
answer: They must adopt the security measures within two years from the date this Act entered into force.

evidence.title: Act No. 69/2018 Coll. on Cybersecurity
evidence.quote: Within two years from the date of the entry into force of this Act, the operator of essential service included in the registry of operators of essential services pursuant to Paragraph 5 is obliged to adopt security measures pursuant to Article 20.

question: If there is reasonable ground to believe that a digital service provider in the electronic communications sector does not meet cybersecurity requirements, who carries out the inspection, and which ministry is listed for that sector?
answer: The Authority carries out the inspection when there is reasonable ground to believe the provider does not meet the Act’s requirements. The Ministry of Transport and Construction of the Slovak Republic is listed for electronic communications.

history.content: How long is the basic annual leave?
The basic leave is at least four weeks [1].

question: And for someone who turns 33 this year?
answer: At least five weeks (also for an employee who permanently cares for a child).

evidence.title: Act No. 311/2001 Coll., Labour Code
evidence.quote: The leave of an employee who reaches at least 33 years of age by the end of the relevant calendar year and of an employee who permanently cares for a child shall be at least five weeks.

history.content: A woman is entitled to 34 weeks of maternity leave [1].

question: And if she gives birth to twins?
answer: 43 weeks.

evidence.title: Act No. 311/2001 Coll., Labour Code
evidence.quote: a woman who has given birth to two or more children at the same time is entitled to maternity leave of 43 weeks

history.content: How quickly must a personal data breach be reported to the Office?
No later than 72 hours after the controller becomes aware of it [1].

question: And when do the affected people have to be told?
answer: Without undue delay, when the breach is likely to result in a high risk to their rights and freedoms.

evidence.title: Act No. 18/2018 Coll. on personal data protection
evidence.section: Section 41 Communication of a personal data breach to the data subject
evidence.quote: When the personal data breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall communicate the personal data breach to the data subject without undue delay.
